title: Assistive Mode Toggle + Live Chart ARIA Sweep and Token Contrast Ramp
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Scope: Audit and remediate accessibility gaps across the design system focused on three tied areas: (1) an "assistive mode" toggle pattern that surfaces high-contrast tokens, simplified focus outlines, and reduced motion; (2) ARIA and live-region strategy for streaming/real-time charts so screen reader users have an accurate and non-noisy experience; (3) a contrast ramp proposal for semantic tokens (neutral, interactive, success/warning/error) across light/dark themes to close AA and selected AAA gaps.

Background: Multiple components (buttons, dense tables, streaming charts) show inconsistent focus treatments and token contrast at smaller densities. Recent customer feedback from a financial customer flagged difficulties using the live P&L chart with VoiceOver; internal audits show a handful of tokens failing WCAG AA at 14px body scale in dark theme. This ticket combines a component-level sweep and a systemic token proposal to enable an "assistive mode" toggle that engineering can opt-into via a single flag.

Goals and deliverables:
- Design pattern for Assistive Mode toggle: visual states, accessible label language, preference persistence, and API contract for engineering (a11y=true).
- Token contrast ramp: a recommended delta table (base token -> assistive delta) for neutral/interactive/semantic tokens that meets AA at minimum and has an optional AAA ramp for customers that enable stricter mode.
- Live-chart ARIA guidelines: explicit roles/attributes for streaming updates (aria-live polite vs off, aria-roledescription, concise text alternates), debounce strategy to avoid announcement storms, and a fallback textual summary component for dense streams.
- Component patches: spec-level guidance and component examples (buttons, table rows, chart legends) showing updated focus ring, keyboard target sizes, and contrast token usage.
- Acceptance criteria and a lightweight QA checklist for accessibility engineers and SREs to validate behavior in VoiceOver, NVDA, and ChromeVox.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Assistive Mode is additive and opt-in to avoid regressions for customers who have custom theming. Engineering will add a hook to expose the flag to hosting layers (hosted/dedicated/private).
- We prefer token deltas over introducing new tokens to minimize breakage; however, when deltas are insufficient we will propose a small set of new semantic tokens with migration notes.
- Live-chart announcements must balance completeness vs noise: propose an adaptive debounce that increases summary granularity during high-frequency updates.

Success metrics:
- All targeted token pairs achieve WCAG AA at 14px and 18px scales in both themes when Assistive Mode is on.
- No live-chart announcement spikes reported in 7-day usability lab (target <5 announcements per minute under heavy updates).
- Component snapshot/visual regression suite shows focus outlines present and accessible across densities.

Acceptance criteria (what dev should deliver to consider ticket done):
1) Figma spec pages for Assistive Mode and token ramp with annotated color values and deltas.
2) Component code examples or PR references implementing the assistive token paths for: Button, Table row, Chart legend, and Modal close.
3) ARIA guidance document and a small reference React component (example stories) showing live-chart behavior and a textual summary fallback.
4) QA checklist passed by Accessibility QA and two cross-browser screen reader passes.

Handoff notes for engineering:
- Provide a small runtime flag (context: {a11yMode: boolean}) or CSS class (.rn-assistive-mode) mapping to token deltas.
- Chart runtime should expose an announcements API (announceSummary(payload)) that follows debounce rules in the spec.
- Table virtualization needs a11y-safe focus management (avoid trapping focus off-viewport rows).

Related artifacts and references are in attachments.
